title: Irrelevant Background/Historical Discussion (TMI)
pattern: API documentation bloated with long historical narratives, RFC histories, or design back-and-forths.
why_bad: High cognitive overhead. API consumers must read through essays of historical context to find basic contract rules. It increases code bloat and offers no value to current callers.
detection: Comments containing long narrative paragraphs (over 3 sentences) discussing historical changes, author opinions, or extensive reference citations unrelated to the API contract.
counterexample: A single-sentence contract reference: 'Encodes data to base64 using the standard alphabet defined in RFC 3548.'
fix: Prune historical details; move architectural discussions to design docs or Git commits.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Too Much Information"), Chapter 17 (G8: "Too Much Information").
